MINUTES
  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JUNE 25, 2024

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

An adjourned meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by MAYOR SCHMITZ at 5:04 p.m. in the Council Chamber of City Hall.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit

4.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

None.

5.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  STUDY SESSION MEETING FOR THE PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH (PVDN)
  AND  DAPPLEGRAY  ELEMENTARY  SCHOOL  (LONDON  LANE)
  INTERSECTION IMPROVEMENT PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Conduct a study session to further
  discuss the proposed Palos Verdes Drive North (PVDN) and Dapplegray
  Elementary School Intersection Improvement Project; and, 2) Direct staff to bring
  back a Resolution approving the Project and the Mitigated Negative Declaration
  (MND) and Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program (MMRP) under the
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) at the City Council meeting of August
  13, 2024.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (per the agenda materials),
summarizing the Palos Verdes Drive North (PVDN) and Dapplegray Elementary School
Intersection Project, a Transportation Enhancement and Americans with Disability Act
(ADA) Improvement Project (Project), which would be primarily funded by Measure M of
the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LACMTA).

Willdan / Traffic Engineer Reggie Greene provided a recap and general overview of the
project, including the history, project introduction, project details, and next steps.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN expressed concern about the school drop-off/pick-up
line backing up in the new auxiliary lane. He emphasized that the School District and City
need to collaborate to help address the congestion during school drop-off and pick-up
times.

Palos Verdes Peninsula School District Superintendent Devin Serrano spoke, noting the
District is in support of this project, is working closely with City staff and has done a few
site visits. The community has expressed that student safety must be the number one
priority, both during construction of the project and after work has been completed. She
also noted the School Board is proposing a bond measure with a detailed project list that
includes Dapplegray Elementary School access road enhancements to help alleviate
some of the congestion on Palos Verdes Drive North.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
ADJOURNED MEETING - STUDY SESSION  1
JUNE 25, 2024
 COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN also discussed that since the bike lane minimum width
is three feet including the apron, the seam between the apron and the road must be level
and smooth for biker’s safety.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER inquired about the impact of the trails during
construction. Public Works Director Wahba explained that they will try to keep the trails
open as much as possible, while providing signage and advance notice of any closures
as necessary. She requested that staff communicate with Palos Verdes Horsemens
Association (PVHA) for any closures.

City Manager Grammer explained that the circular drive/access road at Dapplegray
Elementary is school property, therefore Measure M funding could not be applied toward
those improvements, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

MAYOR PRO TEM STEGURA echoed COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN’S concerns
about the bike lane no longer being protected, and about the massing of cars during
school hours.

Discussion ensued about the median being removed, and the fact that the current median
is too small to be considered a pedestrian refuge.

Los Angeles County Sheriff Deputy Derek Clotworthy stated that the new plan looks like
it will be more difficult for people to park illegally near this intersection, and that the plan
looks like emergency vehicles’ ability to maneuver the intersection will be enhanced.

Los Angeles County Assistant Fire Chief Brian Kane agreed with Deputy Clotworthy,
stating that will be more room and space for cars to move out of the way for emergency
vehicles.

City Manager Grammer noted that there would still be some level of congestion on Palos
Verdes Drive North even with these improvements, which will make it difficult for any cars
to speed through the auxiliary lanes at high speeds to get through the intersection.

Public comments were received from Lynn Yen, Anthony Xepoliv, Grant Mogford and
Shelly Vert, expressing their concerns about the project.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN suggested extending the median on the east side of
the intersection to discourage u-turns. He also confirmed with Director Wahba that the
crosswalks will meet all ADA requirements. He also suggested collaborating with the
School District about pedestrian safety during school hours.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  DIRECTION GIVEN TO STAFF TO SCHEDULE A PUBLIC HEARING AT
  THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING OF AUGUST 13, 2024 TO CONSIDER
  APPROVAL OF THE PROJECT AND THE MITIGATED NEGATIVE
  DECLARATION (MND) AND MITIGATION MONITORING AND
  REPORTING PROGRAM (MMRP) UNDER THE CALIFORNIA
  ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT (CEQA); AND TO BRING BACK A
  REPORT AT THE AUGUST 13 MEETING TO ADDRESS THE
  CONCERNS AND SUGGESTIONS PROVIDED AT THE STUDY
  SESSION.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

6.  ADJOURNMENT

At 6:30 pm MAYOR SCHMITZ adjourned the City Council meeting to the regular City
Council meeting at 7:00 p.m.
